answer: Use a slow-start identity ramp: each new identity must send small, evenly spaced requests across several separate time windows before full access. The rule throttles any identity whose timing resembles a sudden ocean swell or a repeated lagoon pattern, and bursty newcomers wait in a hollow queue until smooth. An attacker pays per identity by keeping each one on its own long, low-rate schedule and distinct traffic shape, so every extra identity adds real time and bandwidth cost.
